entry.title: [BIP Proposal] rawtr() Output Script Descriptors
entry.summary:
The rawtr() descriptor, which has been part of Bitcoin Core since version 24.0, had not been officially defined in a Bitcoin Improvement Proposal (BIP) until recently. Pieter Wuille highlighted this oversight in the bips repository on GitHub in March, leading to the creation of a draft for a new BIP now available at [this GitHub page](https://github.com/jeanpablojp/bips/blob/rawtr-descriptor/bip-rawtr.mediawiki). The necessity for this formalization became evident as BIP 390, which permits only the musig() function within tr(), rawtr(), or sp() descriptors, includes test vectors that utilize the rawtr() descriptors, yet no existing BIP formally recognized the expression.
The draft of the new BIP aligns with the formats of BIPs 384 and 385 and introduces test vectors that were developed against the master branch of Bitcoin Core using tools like getdescriptorinfo and deriveaddresses. Interestingly, the first test vector repurposes a key from the first tr() vector of BIP 386, but applies it differently as rawtr() does not tweak the script. Moreover, the musig() vectors are directly taken from BIP 390.
In terms of structural organization, each expression group such as musig() and sp() has been assigned its unique BIP number, as seen with the recent allocations this year. Consequently, the rawtr() descriptor is proposed as a separate BIP instead of being merged into BIP 386. This decision underscores the practice of dedicating one BIP per expression group, a protocol also reflected in Appendix B of BIP 380.
There is an ongoing discussion about partial-descriptors like rawnode() and rawleaf(), specifically addressed in bips PR 1721, although they are not included in the current draft. The community’s input on these drafts and discussions is crucial for refining and finalizing the proposals.
